title: Tenant sandboxing with soft-failover policies and hierarchical quotas
creator: Sofia Patel
description:
Background: Customers on Dedicated require predictable throughput guarantees. Current fleet-level controls reduce collisions but do not sufficiently isolate transient noisy tenants who produce latency spikes or cause KV cache churn. This ticket proposes a tenant-level sandboxing layer that combines soft-failover (graceful degraded routing), per-tenant GPU bandwidth throttles, and hierarchical quota enforcement (project -> tenant -> route).

Goals:
- Provide bounded tail-latency improvements for co-located tenants under noise.
- Enforce quotas at multiple levels so a misbehaving tenant cannot exhaust shared resources.
- Allow controlled soft-failovers to fallback model variants or lower-precision quantized profiles without dropping requests.

Proposed solution overview:
1) Slab fencing: allocate logical slabs of GPU capacity (memory + compute windows) to tenants with lease tokens. Slabs are soft-isolated: best-effort isolation with throttles rather than hard preemption.
2) Bandwidth and KV cache windowing: track per-tenant aggregate GPU memory working set and per-second token emission; when a tenant exceeds a configurable window, apply progressive backpressure then route additional requests to dedicated lower-capacity lanes or model variants.
3) Soft-failover policies: define a policy chain (primary model -> quantized fallback -> remote-hosted fallback -> delayed queue). The platform moves requests down the chain on quota breach or elevated latency risk.
4) Hierarchical quotas: define quota buckets at project, tenant, and route. Quotas are enforced with reservation tokens and a fast-path admit/deny check integrated into the scheduler.
5) Telemetry and throttle controls: expose per-tenant SLO dashboards, throttle events, and an operator dashboard to adjust slab sizes and burst windows.

Architectural decisions and trade-offs:
- Why soft isolation vs strict partitioning: strict partitioning wastes GPU utilization for common underutilized tenants. Soft isolation provides better overall efficiency while limiting cross-tenant risk via progressive throttles and fallbacks.
- Placement complexity: slab fencing introduces additional scheduler constraints. We'll extend the current placement heuristics with a slab-aware cost metric.
- Eviction semantics: prefer degrading to a compatible model variant over preempting running KV caches to reduce error surface for end-users.

Rollout plan:
- Phase 1 (canary): implement slab accounting + passive monitoring and simulate enforcement in dry-run mode for 2 weeks.
- Phase 2 (limited enforcement): enable progressive throttles for 5 pilot customers with explicit opt-in.
- Phase 3 (general availability): enable hierarchical quotas and soft-failover policies for all Dedicated customers with an admin toggle.

Metrics to track: per-tenant p95/p99 latency, cache miss churn, tenant-induced preemptions, percent of requests served by fallback tier, GPU utilization delta after enforcement, number of throttle events per tenant.

Related artifacts: design doc: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INFRA/pages/1234567/GPU+Sandboxing, infra PR (WIP): https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/2048, operator console mockups: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1a2b3c4d-example, experiment dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.company/d/ABCD/tenant-sandboxing

Open questions:
- Default slab sizes for small vs large tenants and how to price them.
- Exact admission control algorithm for hierarchical quotas under bursty traffic.
- Edge-case: how to surface soft-failover to customer-facing SDKs (transparent vs explicit signals).
acceptance_criteria: Slab accounting proto implemented and validated in unit tests
Dry-run mode logs throttle decisions for 100% of relevant requests over 2 weeks
Canary customers observe <25% reduction in p99 tail spikes compared to baseline when enforcement enabled
Operator console displays per-tenant throttle and fallback events with filters
Rollout runbook and customer-facing communication drafted and approved
